title: Redwood Optimize v2: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Release Notes (Nov 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for Redwood Optimize v2 (shipping Nov 2026). Redwood Optimize v2 is the next-generation cost and performance toolkit that helps customers reduce inference unit costs while preserving quality using automated batching, KV/prefix caching guidance, quantization recommendations, and workload-aware routing.

Intended audience: Product, engineering (serving runtime, infra, applied ML), sales enablement, customer success, and partner integrations.

Goals
- Reduce average per-token inference cost for 75% of monitored workloads by >= 20% within 90 days of adoption.
- Provide actionable, low-friction recommendations (1-click or API) for batching, cache and quantization profiles.
- Detect quality regressions introduced by optimization and provide automatic rollback or canary policies.
- Make Optimize v2 available across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments with the same UX and SLO-friendly defaults.

Success metrics (primary)
- Cost savings: median per-token cost delta for customers who enable Optimize v2 (target >= 20%).
- Adoption: % of eligible customers with recommendations accepted (target >= 30% in Q1 post-launch).
- Quality stability: % of accepted recommendations that do not cause measurable regression on evaluation prompt sets (target >= 95%).
- Latency impact: median P95 generation latency delta after applying recommended batching/quantization (target <= +15% P95).

Product scope and PRD summary
- Core features:
  - Workload analyzer: offline and live traffic profiling to infer batching opportunities, cache prefix reuse, and token length distributions.
  - Recommendation engine: ranked config recommendations (batch_size, batching_timeout_ms, cacheable_prefix_patterns, quantization_profile) with estimated cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.
  - One-click / API apply: apply recommended config to a model route with safe rollout (canary, automatic rollback on quality regressions).
  - Eval guardrails: built-in eval harness that runs a customer prompt set (or default prompts) to estimate quality impact before applying changes.
  - Reporting: per-route cost/latency/quality before and after optimization for auditing and billing.

MUST requirements (v2 initial release)
1. Support for recommendations for text-generation and chat routes across the Hosted API.
2. Provide an API endpoint: POST /optimize/recommendations (route_id, window=ISO8601) returning prioritized recommendations and estimated deltas.
3. 1-click apply in Console that creates a canary rollout (5% traffic) and monitors eval guardrails for 24 hours before gradual rollout.
4. Audit logs and change records for every recommendation apply (owner, timestamp, before/after config).
5. Compatibility with dedicated capacity pools: recommendations must include capacity-aware constraints.

SHOULD requirements
- Support private deployments (VPC) in the initial GA window via an agent and APIs with customer-controlled opt-in.
- Support model-specific quantization profiles (4-bit and 8-bit) and surface potential quality delta estimates.
- Provide SDK helper libraries (python/js) to pull recommendations and programmatically accept them.

Design spec (high-level)
- Components:
  - Profiler service (batch): consumes sampling traces from the runtime (prefix reuse, sequence length histograms, KV hit ratios) and stores aggregated metrics in the analyzer DB. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
  - Recommendation engine: rules + ML scoring layer that maps profiler signals to candidate configs and scores by cost/latency/quality estimate. Owner: applied-ml-and-evals.
  - Eval harness: uses the existing eval framework to run canary prompt sets; evaluates BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity metrics and policy-based fail conditions. Owner: applied-ml-and-evals.
  - Rollout controller: integrates with deployment orchestration to create canary splits, monitor metrics and auto-rollback. Owner: eng-platform.
  - Console UI + API: surfaces recommendations, provides 1-click apply, manual overrides and reporting. Owner: eng-developer-experience + product.

API sketches (public and internal)
- POST /api/v1/optimize/recommendations
  Request body: {"route_id": "r_123", "lookback_window": "P7D"}
  Response: list of candidate configs with fields: id, config_yaml, estimated_cost_delta_usd, estimated_latency_delta_ms, quality_risk_score, explanation.

- POST /api/v1/optimize/apply
  Request body: {"recommendation_id": "rec_456", "rollout": {"strategy": "canary", "initial_pct": 5, "monitoring_period_hrs": 24}}
  Response: apply_job_id, status.

Security and privacy considerations
- No customer prompt data leaves the customer-owned cluster in Private deployments; profiler aggregates are privacy-preserving (hashed prefix keys, no raw prompts persisted).
- Recommendations and audit logs must be RBAC-restricted; only route owners and admins may apply.

Roadmap & themes (Q4 2026 - Q2 2027)
- Q4 2026 (Nov GA): Optimize v2 GA for Hosted API, core recommendation engine, Console 1-click apply, canary rollout, basic pricing guidance.
- Q1 2027: Dedicated support GA, private deployment agent beta, SDKs (python/js), model-specific quantization profiles (4-bit), cost-savings dashboards.
- Q2 2027: Auto-scheduling integration with Dedicated (autoscale + burst aware), multi-model routing suggestions, finer-grained eval guardrails (per-customer prompt set profiling).

Pricing & packaging notes
- Core model: Optimize is an add-on that can be purchased as a subscription or enabled on a usage basis. Pricing options for v2:
  - Starter (included): basic recommendations and reporting for up to 3 routes (no one-click apply).
  - Pro (add-on): full recommendations, 1-click apply, canary rollouts, audit logs. Priced as $X/month + percentage-based savings fee (e.g., 10% of estimated monthly token-cost savings tracked by platform).
  - Enterprise: Dedicated & Private deployment pricing via contract (platform fee + enablement + savings fee discounts).
- Notes on billing: savings fee is collected monthly by tracking per-route baseline cost and realized cost after changes. Baseline calculation: 14-day median per-token cost pre-apply.
- Migration path: customers with existing Redwood Optimize (v1) will get an automatic recommendation import; model-specific quantization must be re-evaluated with v2 eval harness before auto-apply.

Release notes — Redwood Optimize v2.0.0 (2026-11-14 GA)
Highlights:
- General availability for Hosted API: workload analyzer, recommendation engine, Console 1-click apply with canary rollouts, and basic cost reporting.
- API: /optimize/recommendations and /optimize/apply endpoints.
- Eval guardrails: default prompt sets and quality risk scoring to prevent naive regression.
- Audit logging for compliance and change history.
- Pricing model and billing integration for Pro customers.

Detailed changes
- New services: profiler-batch, recommendations-api, rollout-controller, eval-service integration.
- Console: new Optimize tab on per-route pages; recommendation panel with estimated deltas and 1-click apply.
- Metrics: added optimize.recommendation.applied, optimize.rollback.count, optimize.savings.estimated_usd (instrumented for SLOs and alerts).

Rollout plan
1. Internal dogfood (Nov 1–7): enable for 10 internal teams and monitor cost/latency/quality.
2. Early access customers (Nov 8–13): invite 15 existing Hosted customers (opt-in).
3. GA (Nov 14): open to all Hosted customers. Pro billing enabled on GA.
4. Post-GA (Nov 14–Dec 31): monitor quality/regressions, iterate on scoring thresholds, and begin Dedicated & Private support workstreams.

Monitoring, SLOs and alerts
- SLOs:
  - Recommendation API availability: 99.95% monthly.
  - Rollout controller success rate: >= 99% successful canary executions (no infra failures).
- Alerts:
  - optimize.rollback.count > 5 in 1 hour -> page oncall (eng-serving-runtime).
  - quality_guardrail.failures > 1% of canary requests -> create incident and auto-rollback.

Known issues and mitigations
- Quantization quality estimates are conservative for models with poor eval coverage; mitigation: require manual review for high quality-risk scores.
- Private deployment agent v1 requires additional network ports (see eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging) — documented in onprem packaging guide.

Owners and contacts
- Product owner: Aisha Patel (product).
- Eng owners: eng-serving-runtime (profiler) — SRE: Michael Chen; applied-ml-and-evals (recommendation scoring) — Ravi Singh; eng-platform (rollout) — Laura Gómez; DX (console) — Priya Nair.

Appendix: Suggested rollout checklist for CS/SEs
1. Identify candidate route(s) with stable traffic and > 10k tokens/day.
2. Run POST /optimize/recommendations with lookback P14D.
3. Review recommended config and estimated deltas with customer; select one or more recommendations.
4. Apply via Console with canary initial_pct=5, monitoring_period_hrs=24.
5. Monitor optimize.savings.estimated_usd and quality_guardrail.* metrics. If rollback triggered, open triage with eng-serving-runtime.
